# miniq specification

miniq is a small in-memory message queue service. Build it from scratch as a Rust crate whose binary is
named `miniq`, and include tests. It uses no network, no files and no wall clock: all state lives in the
process and time is virtual (section 3).

## 1. Protocol

- miniq reads stdin as lines ending in `\n`; a final line without `\n` counts if it is not empty. Every
  line, blank ones included, is one command and gets exactly one response: one JSON object on a single
  line of stdout, ending in `\n`. Responses come in input order, nothing else goes to stdout, and each
  response is written and flushed before the next line is read. At end of input miniq exits with 0.
- A command is a line that is, as a whole, one JSON object with a string member `Command` and the
  command's parameters as further members, for example `{"Command": "PurgeQueue", "QueueName": "jobs"}`.
  All names are case-sensitive. Members a command does not define are ignored. A parameter or attribute
  whose value is `null` is treated as absent. An object that repeats a member name: unspecified behavior.
- Success response: `{"ok": true}` plus exactly the result members listed for the command.
- Failure response: `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`. `code` is one of the
  codes in section 2; `message` is a human-readable string whose text is up to you. The `error` object
  may carry extra members; every other object in a response has exactly the members this document lists.
  A failed command changes no state.
- Parameter types: a *string* is a JSON string; a *boolean* is `true` or `false`; an *integer* is a JSON
  number written without fraction or exponent (`30`, but not `30.0`, `3e1` or `"30"`). Ranges are
  inclusive. Every number in a response is an integer. Member order and whitespace inside a response
  line are free.

content.text:
I made six small commits on `main`. `cargo test` passes and `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean.

| Commit | What changed and why |
|---|---|
| Assert values in request unit tests | `range_is_inclusive` and `shape_errors` only checked `is_ok()` or `is_err()`. They now compare the parsed value and the error code. |
| Build MissingParameter errors in one place | The same message was formatted in two places. It is now `Error::missing_parameter`. |
| Parse the command name into an enum | The broker matched command names as strings. It now matches a `Command` enum parsed once in `Request::parse`, so the dispatch is exhaustive. The unknown-command error is unchanged. |
| Give message ids, receipt handles and arrival positions their own types | All three were bare `u64`. The new `MessageId`, `ReceiptHandle` and `Arrival` types are in `src/ids.rs`. The `m-<n>` and `r-<n>` wire formats now live in one place each. |
| Extract FIFO parameter checks from send_message | `send_message` was about 70 lines. The checks that depend on queue type moved into `fifo_ids`, with the error order unchanged. |
| Collapse nested if-let in the duplicate-send check | Clippy flagged the nesting. A let chain states the two conditions as one. |

I deliberately left a few things alone, because changing them would alter behavior or is a bigger change than this pass:
- **`require` then `.expect("required")`:** Handlers call `Params::require` and then unwrap each value. Fixing this properly would change which error wins when a parameter is both missing and malformed, as SPEC section 2 orders those checks. It needs a design decision from you.
- **`DeadLetterQueue` and `MaxReceiveCount`:** `AttributeUpdate` holds them as two `Option` fields that must be set together. Merging them into one field would move the "given together" check earlier. That changes the error order against the `.fifo` name check.
- **Queue names and seconds:** Queue names are plain `String` keys, and times and timeouts are plain `u64` seconds. Typing them touches most files.

Say if you want any of these done.

I changed nothing for these five findings. In each case the rule does not apply to the line:

- **`message_commands.rs:40-41` (`group_id`, `deduplication_id`):** these are free-text client identifiers. `Params::identifier` has already validated them, and the spec defines no closed set of values.
- **`message_commands.rs:196` (`queue_name`, `handle`):**
  - `queue_name` is a lookup key and is only borrowed. Typing queue names is the larger change I listed above as left alone.
  - `handle` is the raw wire text. It is parsed into a `ReceiptHandle` only after the queue lookup, because SPEC section 2 orders those checks that way. Parsing it earlier would change which error is returned.
- **`error.rs:52` (`missing_parameter`):** `name` is a parameter name used only to build the message text.
- **`request.rs:31` (`from_name`):** this function turns wire text into the `Command` enum, so it is the parser itself.

The work is finished. The six commits are on `main` and the tests pass.
